name: Shechaniah
overview: Shechaniah appears in Scripture primarily as a figure connected to the post-exilic community of Israel, with descendants who returned from Babylonian captivity alongside leaders like Ezra and Zerubbabel. He is identified as a descendant of David (1 Chronicles 3:21-22) and as a Levite among those who returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 8:3, 8:5). Notably, Shechaniah the son of Jehiel confronted Ezra regarding the sin of intermarriage with Gentile wives, urging a call to repentance and separation to restore holiness (Ezra 10:2). Additionally, he is the father of Shemaiah, who served in a leadership role as gatekeeper (Nehemiah 3:29), highlighting the family's ongoing involvement in the spiritual and communal restoration of Israel.
